instrument.name: Modified Ashworth Scale
instrument.purpose: clinician-rated resistance to passive movement / increased muscle tone
instrument.items: depends on number of muscles/joints tested
instrument.administration_time: less than 5 minutes per RMD, depending on muscles/joints tested
equipment: mat table or standardized examination surface
instrument.spasticity_specificity: limited; resistance to passive movement can reflect neural and non-neural factors

rmd.description: Six choices: 0, 1, 1+, 2, 3, 4; quick passive stretch; standardization and training are important.
considerations: Adequate training is required for inter-rater reliability.
Resistance to passive movement is influenced by soft tissue, joint stiffness, persistent muscle activity and stretch-reflex responses.
The scale does not provide a comprehensive measure of spasticity.

eprovide.conditions_of_use: This questionnaire is in the public domain.
eprovide.translation_distribution: Existing translations can be obtained from Mapi Research Trust; fees may apply to a project.

primary_reference.citation: Bohannon RW, Smith MB. Interrater reliability of a modified Ashworth scale of muscle spasticity. Phys Ther. 1987;67(2):206-207.

methodology_reference.citation: Pandyan AD et al. A review of the properties and limitations of the Ashworth and modified Ashworth Scales as measures of spasticity.
methodology_reference.key_warning: MAS grades, especially 1 versus 1+, are ambiguous enough that numeric aggregation should not be invented.
